name: French Onion Soup (Soupe à l'Oignon Gratinée)
headnote: Daniel Gritzer argues that this soup lives or dies on two things, the onions and the stock, and that the cheese and croutons should be a bonus rather than cover for a weak base. His central claim, backed by citations to Soltner, Julia Child and Patricia Wells, is that the near-universal instruction to cook the onions to a very dark mahogany is wrong and risky: the sweet, deep flavor arrives well before that point, and pushing further easily introduces the bitterness behind most bad versions, so he aims for a rich golden brown. He is blunt that this takes one to two hours in butter over gentle heat, not the 15 or 25 minutes most recipes claim, and he rejects the common shortcuts, finding baking soda turns onions into greenish mush with an off flavor and added sugar pushes them to candy sweetness. He prefers cast iron, carbon steel or stainless to enameled pots, which brown the pan rather than the onions and force constant deglazing. Since good store-bought beef stock is hard to find, he says homemade chicken stock or even a decent boxed brand beats it, and he finishes with sherry, thyme, bay, a little fish sauce for depth and cider vinegar for balance.
comment_digest: The most-flagged issue is yield: a reader points out that 1.8 liters of stock plus the onions is roughly eight cups for four servings, and halved the stock for a heartier, more onion-rich soup; another independently agrees the yield is off. Worcestershire is the usual substitution for fish sauce, and the highest-voted review warns it is strong enough that half a teaspoon would be plenty. Soy sauce with dried thyme also works, as does dried thyme with boxed chicken stock, and several readers boost boxed broth with Better Than Bouillon beef base. Caramelizing times run about an hour to an hour and fifteen minutes with frequent deglazing. One reviewer disputes the author directly, saying the photographed onions are far darker than the golden brown the text prescribes and that chicken broth alone gave a pale result. Gritzer replies in the thread explaining why he rejects baking soda.
flags: 'Load More reviews' present, so only part of the 90 reviews is in the paste; the paste includes a 'Most helpful positive review' block and a 'Featured Tweaks' block with vote counts of 1 on a few entries. Several comments end with 'Read More' and may be truncated.
